name.text: Find the mistake in compound proportion

questiontext.text:
\({@w1@}\) artisans in a jua kali workshop make \({@q1@}\) jiko in \({@d1@}\) days. Working at the same rate, how many jiko can \({@w2@}\) artisans make in \({@d2@}\) days?

{@nm@} wrote this working, which has one mistake:

  1. 1 artisan makes \({@q1@} [[if test="is(er=1)"]]\times[[else]]\div[[/if]] {@w1@} = {@nv(sa)@}\) jiko in \({@d1@}\) days.

  2. 1 artisan makes \({@nv(sa)@} [[if test="is(er=2)"]]\times[[else]]\div[[/if]] {@d1@} = {@nv(sb)@}\) jiko in 1 day.

  3. \({@w2@}\) artisans make \({@nv(sb)@} [[if test="is(er=3)"]]\div[[else]]\times[[/if]] {@w2@} = {@nv(sc)@}\) jiko in 1 day.

  4. In \({@d2@}\) days they make \({@nv(sc)@} [[if test="is(er=4)"]]\div[[else]]\times[[/if]] {@d2@} = {@nv(se)@}\) jiko.

(a) Which line has the mistake?

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

(b) How many jiko can they make?

[[input:ans2]] jiko [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]

generalfeedback.text:
The mistake is in line \({@er@}\). [[if test="is(er=1)"]]Line 1 multiplies by the number of artisans: one artisan must make fewer jiko than all of them, so divide.[[elif test="is(er=2)"]]Line 2 multiplies by the number of days: one artisan makes fewer jiko in 1 day than in all the days, so divide.[[elif test="is(er=3)"]]Line 3 divides by the number of artisans: more artisans make more jiko, so multiply.[[else]]Line 4 divides by the number of days: more days give more jiko, so multiply.[[/if]]

The correct working:

  1. 1 artisan makes \({@q1@} \div {@w1@} = {@nv(ca)@}\) jiko in \({@d1@}\) days.

  2. 1 artisan makes \({@nv(ca)@} \div {@d1@} = {@nv(cb)@}\) jiko in 1 day.

  3. \({@w2@}\) artisans make \({@nv(cb)@} \times {@w2@} = {@nv(cc)@}\) jiko in 1 day.

  4. In \({@d2@}\) days they make \({@nv(cc)@} \times {@d2@} = {@nv(Q)@}\) jiko.

In each line ask: should the answer be more or less than the line before?

Grade 12 CBE Core 1.3 / Essential 1.2 (C c; E c): Find the faulty line in a unitary-method solution to a compound proportion problem, then solve it.

truefeedback.text: There is a mistake. Test the last line: \({@w1@}\) artisans for \({@d1@}\) days is \({@w1*d1@}\) artisan-days, and that makes \({@q1@}\) jiko. \({@w2@}\) artisans for \({@d2@}\) days is \({@w2*d2@}\) artisan-days, but the working ends with \({@nv(se)@}\) jiko. In each line ask: should the answer be more or less than the line before?

falsefeedback.text: [[if test="is(ans1=1)"]]Line 1 divides by the \({@w1@}\) artisans to find what 1 artisan makes. One artisan makes fewer jiko than \({@w1@}\) artisans, so dividing is right there.[[elif test="is(ans1=2)"]]Line 2 divides by the \({@d1@}\) days to find what is made in 1 day. Fewer jiko are made in 1 day than in \({@d1@}\) days, so dividing is right there.[[elif test="is(ans1=3)"]]Line 3 multiplies by the \({@w2@}\) artisans. \({@w2@}\) artisans make more jiko than 1 artisan, so multiplying is right there.[[else]]Line 4 multiplies by the \({@d2@}\) days. More jiko are made in \({@d2@}\) days than in 1 day, so multiplying is right there.[[/if]] A line can use the right operation on a wrong number: look for the line whose operation itself goes the wrong way.

truefeedback.text: That is {@nm@}'s answer, which has a mistake in it.
You changed the number of artisans but not the number of days.
You changed the number of days but not the number of artisans.

falsefeedback.text: Check with artisan-days. \({@q1@}\) jiko take \({@w1@} \times {@d1@} = {@w1*d1@}\) artisan-days. Your \({@ans2@}\) jiko would come from \({@w2@} \times {@d2@} = {@w2*d2@}\) artisan-days. The number of jiko for each artisan-day must be the same both times.
